{{Short description|Class of distance functions defined between probability distributions}}

In [[probability theory]], '''integral probability metrics''' are types of [[metric (mathematics)|distance functions]] between [[Probability distribution|probability distributions]], defined by how well a class of functions can distinguish the two distributions. Many important [[statistical distance|statistical distances]] are integral probability metrics, including the [[Wasserstein metric|Wasserstein-1 distance]] and the [[Total variation distance of probability measures|total variation distance]]. In addition to theoretical importance, integral probability metrics are widely used in areas of [[statistics]] and [[machine learning]].

The name "integral probability metric" was given by German statistician Alfred Müller;<ref name="mueller">{{cite journal |last1=Müller |first1=Alfred |title=Integral Probability Metrics and Their Generating Classes of Functions |journal=Advances in Applied Probability |date=June 1997 |volume=29 |issue=2 |pages=429–443 |doi=10.2307/1428011|jstor=1428011 |s2cid=124648603 }}</ref> the distances had also previously been called "metrics with a {{math| ''ζ''}}-structure."<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zolotarev |first1=V. M. |title=Probability Metrics |journal=Theory of Probability & Its Applications |date=January 1984 |volume=28 |issue=2 |pages=278–302 |doi=10.1137/1128025}}</ref>

== Definition ==
Integral probability metrics (IPMs) are distances on the space of distributions over a set <math>\mathcal X</math>, defined by a class <math>\mathcal{F}</math> of real-valued functions on <math>\mathcal{X}</math> as
<math display=block>D_{\mathcal{F}}(P, Q) = \sup_{f \in \mathcal F} \big| \mathbb E_{X \sim P} f(X) - \mathbb E_{Y \sim Q} f(Y) \big| = \sup_{f \in \mathcal F} \big| P f - Q f \big|;</math>
here the notation {{math| ''P'' ''f''}} refers to the expectation of {{math| ''f''}} under the distribution {{math| ''P''}}. The absolute value in the definition is unnecessary, and often omitted, for the usual case where for every <math>f \in \mathcal F</math> its negation <math>-f</math> is also in <math>\mathcal F</math>.

The functions {{math|''f''}} being optimized over are sometimes called "critic" functions;<ref name="wgan">{{Cite journal |last1=Arjovsky |first1=Martin |last2=Chintala |first2=Soumith |last3=Bottou |first3=Léon |date=2017-07-17 |title=Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks |url=https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/arjovsky17a.html |journal=International Conference on Machine Learning |language=en |publisher=PMLR |pages=214–223}}</ref> if a particular <math>f^* \in \mathcal F</math> achieves the supremum, it is often termed a "witness function"<ref name="mmd">{{cite journal |last1=Gretton |first1=Arthur |last2=Borgwardt |first2=Karsten M. |last3=Rasche |first3=Malte J. |last4=Schölkopf |first4=Bernhard |last5=Smola |first5=Alexander |title=A Kernel Two-Sample Test |journal=Journal of Machine Learning Research |date=2012 |volume=13 |pages=723–773 |url=https://jmlr.org/papers/volume13/gretton12a/gretton12a.pdf}}</ref> (it "witnesses" the difference in the distributions). These functions try to have large values for samples from {{math|''P''}} and small (likely negative) values for samples from {{math|''Q''}}; this can be thought of as a weaker version of [[classification rule|classifers]], and indeed IPMs can be interpreted as the optimal [[statistical risk|risk]] of a particular classifier.{{r|on-ipms|at=sec. 4}}

The choice of <math>\mathcal F</math> determines the particular distance; more than one <math>\mathcal F</math> can generate the same distance.<ref name="mueller"/>

For any choice of <math>\mathcal F</math>, <math>D_{\mathcal F}</math> satisfies all the definitions of a metric except that we may have <math>D_{\mathcal F}(P, Q) = 0</math> for some {{math| ''P'' ≠ ''Q''}}; this is variously termed a "[[Metric space#pseudometric|pseudometric]]" or a "semimetric" depending on the community. For instance, using the class <math>\mathcal F = \{ x \mapsto 0 \}</math> which only contains the zero function, <math>D_{\mathcal F}(P, Q)</math> is identically zero. <math>D_{\mathcal F}</math> is a metric if and only if <math>\mathcal F</math> [[Separating set|separates points]] on the space of probability distributions, i.e. for any {{math|''P'' ≠ ''Q''}} there is some <math>f \in \mathcal F</math> such that <math>P f \ne Q f</math>;<ref name="mueller"/> most, but not all, common particular cases satisfy this property.

== Examples ==
All of these examples are metrics except when noted otherwise.

* The [[Wasserstein metric|Wasserstein-1 distance]] (also called [[earth mover's distance]]), via its [[Wasserstein metric#Dual representation of W1|dual representation]], has <math>\mathcal F</math> the set of 1-[[Lipschitz continuity|Lipschitz]] functions.
* The related Dudley metric is generated by the set of ''bounded'' 1-Lipschitz functions.
* The [[Total variation distance of probability measures|total variation distance]] can be generated by <math>\mathcal F = \{ f : \mathcal X \to \{0, 1\} \}</math>, so that <math>\mathcal F</math> is a set of [[indicator function]]s for any event, or by the larger class <math>\mathcal F = \{ f : \mathcal X \to [0, 1] \}</math>.
* The closely related [[Radon measure#Metric space structure|Radon metric]] is generated by ''continuous'' functions bounded in {{math| [-1, 1]}}. Total variation and the Radon metric coincide (up to scaling) on [[Polish space]]s.{{r|mueller|at=sec. 5.2}} <ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Chou |first1=Yu-Lin |title=On Almost Uniform Continuity of Borel Functions on Polish Metric Spaces |date=2020 |class=math.FA |eprint=2008.00786}}</ref>
* The Kolmogorov metric used in the [[Kolmogorov-Smirnov test]] has a function class of indicator functions, <math>\mathcal F = \{ 1_{(-\infty, t]} : t \in \mathbb R \}</math>.
* The [[Kernel embedding of distributions#Measuring distance between distributions|kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MMD)]] has <math>\mathcal F</math> the [[unit ball]] in a [[reproducing kernel Hilbert space]]. This distance is particularly easy to estimate from samples, requiring no optimization; it is a proper metric exactly when the underlying kernel is ''characteristic.''<ref>{{Cite journal|first1=Kenji |last1=Fukumizu |first2=Arthur |last2=Gretton |first3=Xiaohui |last3=Sun |first4=Bernhard |last4=Schölkopf |author-link4=Bernhard Schölkopf |year=2007 |title=Kernel Measures of Conditional Dependence |journal=[[Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems|Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems]] |volume=20 |url=https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2007/hash/3a0772443a0739141292a5429b952fe6-Abstract.html}}</ref>
* The [[energy distance]], as a special case of the maximum mean discrepancy,<ref>{{Cite journal|first1=Dino |last1=Sejdinovic |first2=Bharath |last2=Sriperumbudur |first3=Arthur |last3=Gretton |first4=Kenji |last4= Fukumizu |year=2013| title=Equivalence of distance-based and RKHS-based statistics in hypothesis testing |journal= The Annals of Statistics| volume=41|number=5|pages=2263–2291|doi=10.1214/13-aos1140|arxiv=1207.6076|s2cid=8308769 }}</ref> is generated by the unit ball in a ''particular'' reproducing kernel Hilbert space.
* Defining <math>\mathcal F</math> by functions with a bounded [[Sobolev space|Sobolev norm]] gives a useful distance for [[generative artificial intelligence|generative modeling]], among other applications.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mroueh |first1=Youssef |last2=Li |first2=Chun-Liang |last3=Sercu |first3=Tom |last4=Raj |first4=Anant |last5=Cheng |first5=Yu |title=Sobolev GAN |journal=[[International Conference on Learning Representations]] |date=2018 |arxiv=1711.04894 |url=https://openreview.net/forum?id=SJA7xfb0b}}</ref>
* Functions with bounded [[Besov space|Besov norm]] generalize many other forms of IPM and are amenable to theoretical analysis.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Uppal |first1=Ananya |last2=Singh |first2=Shashank |last3=Póczos |first3=Barnabás |title=Nonparametric Density Estimation & Convergence Rates for GANs under Besov IPM Losses |journal=[[Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems|Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems]] |date=2019 |volume=32 |url=https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2019/hash/fb09f481d40c4d3c0861a46bd2dc52c0-Abstract.html |arxiv=1902.03511}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Uppal |first1=Ananya |last2=Singh |first2=Shashank |last3=Póczos |first3=Barnabás |title=Robust Density Estimation under Besov IPM Losses |journal=[[Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems|Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems]] |date=2020 |volume=33 |pages=5345–5355 |url=https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2020/hash/39d4b545fb02556829aab1db805021c3-Abstract.html |arxiv=2004.08597}}</ref>
* Many variants of [[generative adversarial network|generative adversarial networks]] and [[classification rule|classifer]]-based [[two-sample hypothesis testing|two-sample tests]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kim |first1=Ilmun |last2=Ramdas |first2=Aaditya |last3=Singh |first3=Aarti |last4=Wasserman |first4=Larry |author-link4=Larry A. Wasserman |title=Classification accuracy as a proxy for two-sample testing |journal=[[The Annals of Statistics]] |date=February 2021 |volume=49 |issue=1 |doi=10.1214/20-AOS1962 |arxiv=1703.00573 |s2cid=17668083 }}</ref><ref name="c2st">{{cite journal |last1=Lopez-Paz |first1=David |last2=Oquab |first2=Maxime |title=Revisiting Classifier Two-Sample Tests |journal=[[International Conference on Learning Representations]] |date=2017 |arxiv=1610.06545 |url=https://openreview.net/forum?id=SJkXfE5xx}}</ref> use a "neural net distance"<ref name="gen-and-eq">{{cite journal |last1=Arora |first1=Sanjeev |author-link1=Sanjeev Arora (computer scientist) |last2=Ge |first2=Rong |last3=Liang |first3=Yingyu |last4=Ma |first4=Tengyu |last5=Zhang |first5=Yi |title=Generalization and Equilibrium in Generative Adversarial Nets (GANs) |date=2017 |journal=[[International Conference on Machine Learning]]|arxiv=1703.00573 }}</ref><ref name="minimax-nns">{{cite journal |last1=Ji |first1=Kaiyi |last2=Liang |first2=Yingbin |title=Minimax Estimation of Neural Net Distance |journal=[[Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems|Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems]] |date=2018|arxiv=1811.01054 }}</ref> where <math>\mathcal F</math> is a class of [[artificial neural network|neural networks]]; these are not metrics for typical fixed-size networks, but could be for other classifiers. For [[Wasserstein GAN]]s in particular, it has been argued that analysis in terms of this distance and not the Wasserstein they approximate is very important to the behavior of these models.<ref name="gen-and-eq"/><ref>{{cite arXiv|eprint=2103.01678 |last1=Stanczuk |first1=Jan |last2=Etmann |first2=Christian |author3=Lisa Maria Kreusser |last4=Schönlieb |first4=Carola-Bibiane |title=Wasserstein GANs Work Because They Fail (To Approximate the Wasserstein Distance) |year=2021 |class=stat.ML }}</ref><ref>{{ cite arXiv|eprint=1910.03875 |last1=Mallasto |first1=Anton |last2=Montúfar |first2=Guido |last3=Gerolin |first3=Augusto |title=How Well do WGANs Estimate the Wasserstein Metric? |year=2019 |class=cs.LG }}</ref>

== Relationship to {{math|''f''}}-divergences ==
The [[F-divergence|{{math|''f''}}-divergences]] are probably the best-known way to measure dissimilarity of probability distributions. It has been shown{{r|on-ipms|at=sec. 2}} that the only functions which are both IPMs and {{math|''f''}}-divergences are of the form <math>c \, \operatorname{TV}(P, Q)</math>, where <math>c \in [0, \infty]</math> and <math>\operatorname{TV}</math> is the total variation distance between distributions.

One major difference between {{math|''f''}}-divergences and most IPMs is that when {{math|''P''}} and {{math|''Q''}} have disjoint support, all {{math|''f''}}-divergences take on a constant value;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.stackexchange.com/a/621718 |title=Computing Jensen-Shannon Divergence between discrete and continuous distribution |first1=Danica J. |last1=Sutherland |accessdate=18 July 2023 |publisher=Stack Exchange Network}}</ref> by contrast, IPMs where functions in <math>\mathcal F</math> are "smooth" can give "partial credit." For instance, consider the sequence <math>\delta_{1/n}</math> of [[Dirac measure]]s at {{math|1/''n''}}; this sequence [[convergence of random variables#convergence in distribution|converges in distribution]] to <math>\delta_0</math>, and many IPMs satisfy <math>D_{\mathcal F}(\delta_{1/n}, \delta_0) \to 0</math>, but no nonzero {{math|''f''}}-divergence can satisfy this. That is, many IPMs are [[Continuous function#Continuous functions between topological spaces|continuous]] in [[Comparison of topologies|weaker topologies]] than {{math|''f''}}-divergences. This property is sometimes of substantial importance,<ref name="towards-principled-gans">{{cite journal |first1=Martin |last1=Arjovsky |first2=Léon |last2=Bettou |author-link2=Léon Bottou |title=Towards Principled Methods for Training Generative Adversarial Networks |journal=[[International Conference on Learning Representations]] |year=2017 |arxiv=1701.04862}}</ref> although other options also exist, such as considering {{math|''f''}}-divergences between distributions [[convolution of probability distributions|convolved]] with continuous noise<ref name="towards-principled-gans"/><ref>{{cite journal|arxiv=1610.04490|at=Appendix C |first1=Casper Kaae |last1=Sønderby |last2=Caballero |first2=Jose |last3=Theis |first3=Lucas |last4=Shi |first4=Wenzhe |last5=Huszár |first5=Ferenc |title=Amortised MAP Inference for Image Super-resolution |year=2017 |journal=[[International Conference on Learning Representations]] }}</ref> or informal convolutions between f-divergences and integral probability metrics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Stein |first1=Viktor |last2=Neumayer |first2=Sebastian |last3=Rux |first3=Nicolaj |last4=Steidl |first4=Gabriele |date=2025-05-03 |title=Wasserstein gradient flows for Moreau envelopes of f-divergences in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/10.1142/S0219530525500162 |journal=Analysis and Applications |volume=24 |language=en |pages=21–65 |doi=10.1142/S0219530525500162 |issn=0219-5305|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Birrell |first1=Jeremiah |last2=Dupuis |first2=Paul |last3=Katsoulakis |first3=Markos A. |last4=Pantazis |first4=Yannis |last5=Rey-Bellet |first5=Luc |date=2022-01-01 |title=(f, Γ)-Divergences: interpolating between f-divergences and integral probability metrics |url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.5555/3586589.3586628 |journal=J. Mach. Learn. Res. |volume=23 |issue=1 |pages=39:1816–39:1885 |issn=1532-4435}}</ref>

== Estimation from samples ==
Because IPM values between discrete distributions are often sensible, it is often reasonable to estimate <math>D_{\mathcal F}(P, Q)</math> using a simple "plug-in" estimator: <math>D_{\mathcal F}(\hat P, \hat Q)</math> where <math>\hat P</math> and <math>\hat Q</math> are [[empirical measure]]s of sample sets. These empirical distances can be computed exactly for some classes <math>\mathcal F</math>;<ref name="on-ipms">{{cite arXiv |eprint=0901.2698 |last1=Sriperumbudur |first1=Bharath K. |last2=Fukumizu |first2=Kenji |last3=Gretton |first3=Arthur |last4=Schölkopf |first4=Bernhard |author-link4=Bernhard Schölkopf |last5=Lanckriet |first5=Gert R. G. |title=On integral probability metrics, φ-divergences and binary classification |year=2009 |class=cs.IT }}</ref> estimation quality varies depending on the distance, but can be [[minimax estimator|minimax-optimal]] in certain settings.<ref name="minimax-nns" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tolstikhin |first1=Ilya O. |last2=Sriperumbudur |first2=Bharath K. |last3=Schölkopf |first3=Bernhard |author3-link=Bernhard Schölkopf |title=Minimax Estimation of Maximum Mean Discrepancy with Radial Kernels |journal=[[Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems|Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems]] |year=2016 |volume=29 |url=https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2016/hash/5055cbf43fac3f7e2336b27310f0b9ef-Abstract.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|eprint=1802.08855 |last1=Singh |first1=Shashank |last2=Póczos |first2=Barnabás |title=Minimax Distribution Estimation in Wasserstein Distance |year=2018 |class=math.ST }}</ref>

When exact maximization is not available or too expensive, another commonly used scheme is to [[Training, validation, and test data sets|divide the samples]] into "training" sets (with empirical measures <math>\hat P_\mathit{train}</math> and <math>\hat Q_\mathit{train}</math>) and "test" sets (<math>\hat P_\mathit{test}</math> and <math>\hat Q_\mathit{test}</math>), find <math>\hat f</math> approximately maximizing <math>\big| \hat P_\mathit{train} f - \hat Q_\mathit{train} f \big|</math>, then use <math>\big| \hat P_\mathit{test} \hat f - \hat Q_\mathit{test} \hat f \big|</math> as an estimate.<ref name="demystifying">{{cite journal|arxiv=1801.01401 |last1=Bińkowski |first1=Mikołaj |last2=Sutherland |first2=Danica J. |last3=Arbel |first3=Michael |last4=Gretton |first4=Arthur |title=Demystifying MMD GANs |year=2018 |url=https://openreview.net/forum?id=r1lUOzWCW |journal=[[International Conference on Learning Representations]] }}</ref><ref name="c2st"/><ref>{{cite journal|arxiv=2002.09116 |last1=Liu |first1=Feng |last2=Xu |first2=Wenkai |last3=Lu |first3=Jie |last4=Zhang |first4=Guangquan |last5=Gretton |first5=Arthur |last6=Sutherland |first6=Danica J. |title=Learning Deep Kernels for Non-Parametric Two-Sample Tests |year=2020 |url=https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/liu20m.html |journal=[[International Conference on Machine Learning]] |pages=6316–6326 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kübler |first1=Jonas M. |last2=Jitkrittum |first2=Wittawat |last3=Schölkopf |first3=Bernhard |author3-link=Bernhard Schölkopf |last4=Muandent |first4=Krikamol |title=A Witness Two-Sample Test |journal=International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics |year=2021 |pages=1403–1419 |url=https://proceedings.mlr.press/v151/kubler22a.html |arxiv=2102.05573}}</ref> This estimator can possibly be [[consistent estimator|consistent]], but has a negative bias.{{r|demystifying|at=thm. 2}} In fact, no [[unbiased estimator]] can exist for any IPM,{{r|demystifying|at=thm. 3}} although there is for instance an unbiased estimator of the ''squared'' maximum mean discrepancy.{{r|mmd}}
